ranking.note: Raised to P1: fixes an index startup race and stale-data-during-reorg window and is the stated prerequisite for out-of-process indexes (#10102) and shared chain sync (#15719), so it cannot sit level with the speedups it enables.

Raised to P1 and moved up six places: a corrupt txindex silently answering 'transaction not found' is exactly the wrong-answer case this category ranks first, and the bug was reproduced, not just claimed.
Raised to P1: same data-integrity class as #36789 but broader, turning masked index/block-read corruption into explicit fatal errors.
Kept P2 but placed ahead of #26966 because it is the extracted foundation that the parallel-sync PR builds on.

inconsistencies: #34132 and #36789 overlap: both make txindex lookup failures stop masking storage corruption. #36789 is the narrow, demonstrated fix and should be reviewed first; #34132's broader fatal-error policy (much of it in coins/dbwrapper, i.e. validation territory) should then be assessed against whatever lands.

Chain: #34489 (batch index db writes) is the extracted foundation for #26966 (parallel index sync); the author states they proceed alongside each other. Review #34489 first or the parallelization will be re-based on moving ground.

#24230 and #35474 both remove node-internal/global coupling from the index framework for the same multiprocess goal (#10102). They will conflict; #24230 is the larger, correctness-bearing one and should set the direction, with #35474 rebased onto it.

#36480 (block-sequence keys for txospenderindex) explicitly prepares that index for pruned mode, which is the capability #36002 adds for txindex and which #36629 claims already; the three should be read together so the pruned-mode lookup convention (candidate hashes + getblockfrompeer) is settled once.
result.notes: Three P1s all rest on the category's first criterion (an index that returns wrong answers or loses integrity) or on unblocking the framework work the rest of the list depends on. The P2 block is deliberately wide: it spans a long-requested feature (#36002), two sync-performance PRs in a dependency chain, a new index with a stated external consumer (#36629), and a 33% disk-footprint cut (#36480) — all durable user-visible value, none with a correctness consequence if deferred a cycle. #34132's centre of gravity is in coins/dbwrapper, which this category calls validation; only its txindex and block-read portions are judged here.
